equity_bridge.item: Non-recourse debt economically borne by NCI / tax-equity partners (not an AES claim), est. 30% of 26,903
equity_bridge.note: Flows are attributable-only, so deducting 100% of consolidated non-recourse debt would charge AES for partners' leverage. The share is not disclosed; two independent anchors bound it: (1) the transaction's stated EV of ~$33.4bn against ~$10.7bn equity implies ~$22.7bn of net claims at Dec-2025 vs $28.5bn consolidated net debt, i.e. ~20% of consolidated debt treated as partners'; (2) the FY2025 Adjusted-PTC bridge (attributable EBITDA 2,871 -> Adjusted PTC 1,547) shows AES bearing only ~$1.3bn of the $2.6bn consolidated D&A + net interest, i.e. roughly half. 30% of non-recourse (24% of gross debt) is set between the two, nearer the conservative end. Each 10pp of non-recourse debt is ~$3.8/share.

equity_bridge.item: Loan receivable at book (interest income excluded from Adjusted EBITDA; matching-asset rule)
equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet, loan receivable net of allowance $690m. Interest income ($287m FY2025) is outside the EBITDA line and is not re-added; its source asset enters the bridge once. Debt service reserves ($124m) secure non-recourse debt and are excluded.

scenario_narratives.base: Standalone (deal-breaks) central case. The 5.7 GW under construction and 12 GW signed backlog commission through 2029, lifting attributable Adjusted EBITDA from $2.9bn (FY2025) to ~$3.8bn (FY2026E, three quarters reported) and ~$4.9bn by Y4; AES-funded capex falls from ~36% of revenue to ~20% by Y5 as the build-out normalises, so owner FCF is negative for roughly three more years (FY2026-FY2028) before turning positive. Cash tax ramps from 13% to 21% as wind/solar credits phase out. Terminal value binds at the 20x cap (Gordon at 7%/2.5% would be ~23x). The bridge nets consolidated net debt of $31.3bn against an explicit $8.1bn estimate of the non-recourse debt partners bear and $0.7bn of loan receivables; the result is a modest positive equity value well below the $15.00 offer -- which is the point: the consortium, with infrastructure-fund capital at a lower cost than public equity, is paying close to the uncapped Gordon value, consistent with the board's statement that the standalone path required dividend cuts or dilution.
scenario_narratives.bull: Standalone upside: data-centre PPAs sustain 4 GW/yr of new contracts, backlog is fully safe-harboured, partner capital keeps funding ~45% of consolidated capex, margin reaches 31% on mix and cash tax stays under 20% on storage ITCs. This is the case the acquirer is underwriting with cheaper capital; on public-market cost of capital it lands around the offer price.
scenario_narratives.bear: Standalone downside: credit phase-out, FEOC rules and interconnection delays stall the pipeline after the current backlog; margins drift down; capex stays elevated longer; the dividend is cut and equity is issued. Equity value falls to zero or below on a fully-consolidated-debt view -- the business survives (contracted cash flows service the project debt) but AES common is an out-of-the-money option on a deleveraging. Any scenario printing a negative intrinsic value here is a finding, not a rounding error: it says the equity's value absent the deal rests on partner capital and refinancing continuing to be available.

corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv_calculation: 0.92 x 14.78 (PV of consideration plus expected interim dividend) + 0.08 x 8.47 (floored standalone weighted IV) = 13.60 + 0.68 = 14.27 USD/share
corporate_action.reading: While the merger is live the actionable value is deal_weighted_iv, not the standalone weighted IV: the stock is a merger-arbitrage instrument with a ~1% gross spread to the $15.00 consideration and a realisable-value ceiling at the consideration plus any interim dividend. The standalone layer is what a holder owns if the deal breaks, and is the reason the arb spread is not zero.
corporate_action.deal_break_value_note: Standalone probability-weighted IV with the bear scenario floored at zero: 0.30 x 0 + 0.50 x 8.41 + 0.20 x 21.32 = 8.47. The engine's unfloored weighted_iv (2.76) carries the bear at -19.02, but a holder cannot lose more than the share price, so the floored figure is the right break value for the arb arithmetic. Using the unfloored figure instead gives a deal-weighted IV of 13.82.
corporate_action.spread_at_valuation_date: Consideration 15.00 vs price at inputs.price_as_of: gross spread ~0.9%, ~1.5% including the expected interim dividend, over ~0.23 years to the modelled close (~6-7% annualised); market-implied completion probability ~95% against a ~12.5 undisturbed break value

valuation_philosophy.summary: AES is valued in two layers because a signed, shareholder-approved, largely-cleared cash merger changes what 'intrinsic value' means for a holder today. Layer 1 (this engine's three scenarios) is the standalone owner-FCF DCF on an attributable basis: AES's own NCI-adjusted Adjusted EBITDA, AES-funded capex, a cash tax rate that ramps as renewable credits phase out, consolidated net debt reduced by an explicit, bounded estimate of partner-borne non-recourse debt, 7% USD WACC, 20x terminal cap. It says standalone AES equity is worth materially less than $15 -- plausibly single digits in the base case and nothing in the bear -- because three more years of negative owner FCF sit in front of a terminal value that must then clear $23bn of attributable net claims, which is exactly the capital-structure stress the board cited when it recommended the sale. Layer 2 (`corporate_action`) is deal-completes vs deal-breaks: 92% x PV of the $15.00 consideration plus 8% x the standalone weighted IV. The two reconcile as follows: the consortium is paying roughly the uncapped Gordon value of the base case at a 7% discount rate (~9x forward attributable EBITDA), i.e. it is monetising for AES shareholders a cost-of-capital advantage that public equity holders could not. The $15.00 is therefore both the ceiling on realisable value and a fair-to-full price against the standalone DCF; there is no case for owning AES above the deal-weighted value, and at a ~1% spread the stock is correctly priced as low-risk merger arbitrage, not as an undervalued utility.
key_risks_to_valuation: Deal break (FERC Burdensome Condition, Ohio OCC rehearing imposing ring-fencing the buyer rejects, MAE, litigation) -- the stock would re-rate toward the standalone layer, i.e. a 30-50% drawdown from the deal price on the base case and more on the bear

Attributable-debt allocation: the share of non-recourse debt that partners bear is undisclosed; each 10pp of non-recourse debt is ~$3.8/share on the standalone value. The 30% used is bounded by the transaction EV (~20%) and the Adjusted-PTC bridge (~50%)
Tax-credit policy: the 2025 Act's wind/solar phase-out and FEOC restrictions govern post-2027 project economics and the cash tax ramp; faster phase-out is bear, durable storage ITC is bull

Partner-capital availability: the capex path assumes tax-equity/NCI funding continues at ~40-45% of consolidated capex; a tax-equity market retreat pushes AES-funded capex up and FCF turn-positive out past FY2028
Latin America (Chile/Colombia hydrology, Argentine peso, Panama, El Salvador) and PREPA (Title III bankruptcy, AES Ilumina default) -- recurring FX and counterparty losses ($79m FX loss in 2025)
Terminal multiple: the 20x FCF cap binds in base and bull; at 15x the base standalone value falls by roughly a third

Timing: if the deal slips to the June-2027 outside date the arb return compresses (offset partly by an extra $0.176 dividend); if it closes early 2027 the ticker dies and this file must be retired per the AVB/EA precedent

This is a finding, not an artefact -- in the deal-breaks-and-credits-phase-out world AES common is an out-of-the-money option on deleveraging, which is consistent with the board's own statement that the standalone path needed a dividend cut and/or substantial equity issuance. inputs.debt_detail: 2026-09-30 balance sheet: recourse debt 6,361 (all non-current; nil current) + non-recourse debt 2,950 current + 23,953 non-current = 33,264 gross. Cash and equivalents 1,972 (restricted cash excluded; it secures non-recourse covenants). Consolidated net debt 31,292. Noncontrolling interests 5,071 and redeemable stock of subsidiaries 3,100 are NOT deducted in the bridge because the flows are already attributable-only (see nci_treatment).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, equity beta 1.1 (pre-deal AES beta, LatAm and development exposure above a pure regulated utility) -> cost of equity ~9.7%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~6.0% (BBB- recourse notes 2025-26 issuance ~5.5-6.5%; non-recourse project debt similar), after-tax ~5.1% at the low cash tax rate. Attributable net claims ~23bn vs deal equity 10.7bn -> D/V ~68%. Weighted ~6.6%; rounded UP to 7.0% for the Latin American (Chile, Colombia, Panama, DR, Argentina, El Salvador) and PREPA counterparty exposure. Same WACC in every scenario -- scenario risk is charged in the flows, not stacked on the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease principal is not deducted from the flows and the lease charge sits inside Adjusted EBITDA as operating cost where it is an operating lease. Total lease liabilities were $1,165m at 2025-12-31 (FY2025 10-K) -- 3.5% of gross debt; they are NOT added to total_debt because the component build already charges lease cost through the EBITDA margin (ASC 842 operating lease expense is inside cost of sales/G&A for a US GAAP filer) and finance-lease liabilities are immaterial. Stated so the reader knows they were considered, not forgotten.
inputs.nci_treatment: ATTRIBUTABLE FLOWS, NCI CHARGED ONCE (owner-fcf-adaptations section (c), route 1). AES's consolidated statements are heavily diluted by tax-equity investors and minority JV partners (CDPQ 30% of AES Ohio/Indiana, GIP in Chile Renovables, TotalEnergies in Puerto Rico, project-level partners): FY2025 consolidated net income was $162m vs $910m attributable to AES; the NCI absorbed $748m of HLBV losses. The build therefore uses AES's OWN NCI-adjusted 'Adjusted EBITDA' as the EBITDA line (FY2025 $2,871m = consolidated adjusted EBITDA $3,695m less the $824m 'adjustment for noncontrolling interests and redeemable stock of subsidiaries'; 9M-2026 $2,815m less $713m NCI). Capex is AES-FUNDED capex: consolidated capex less sales/contributions to NCI and preferred shares issued at subsidiaries (FY2025: 5,929 - 2,084 - 437 - 992 = 2,416, 19.7% of revenue; FY2024 48%; FY2023 41.5%; 9M-2026 37%). Tax attributes ($1,540m FY2025) are deliberately NOT added to EBITDA -- the bulk is the consideration tax-equity partners receive for the capital netted against capex, so including both would double count; AES's own retained credits show up instead as the low cash tax rate (FY2025 cash taxes paid $227m on ~$1.7bn of attributable EBIT = ~13%). Because flows are attributable, NCI book value (5,071 + 3,100 redeemable) is NOT deducted. Debt is the remaining asymmetry: 100% of non-recourse debt is consolidated but partners bear part of it economically -- that share is added back as an explicit equity_bridge item (see there) rather than buried.
inputs.fcf_base_note: inputs.last_fcf (-1,643) is the CONSOLIDATED owner FCF per the house definition (OCF 4,306 - capex 5,929 - SBC 20) and is reported for auditability only. It is not a usable base: it is 100%-consolidated (includes partners' share and $1,028m of tax-credit-transfer cash passed to NCI) and sits mid build-out (5.7 GW under construction). The forward FCF is built from the attributable components above.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build on an ATTRIBUTABLE basis (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-tech, with the adaptations for NCI and leases), run through the Drivers/build-dcf engine. CORPORATE ACTION: AES is the target of a signed all-cash merger at $15.00/share (Horizon Parent L.P.; GIP/BlackRock + EQT Infrastructure VI, with CalPERS and QIA), shareholder-approved 2026-06-26, HSR/CFIUS/EU/PUCO/NY-PSC cleared, FERC and customary conditions outstanding, outside date 2027-06-01 (two 3-month extensions available). Per the dcf-methods routing row for a live takeover and the house precedent for pending-but-unclosed cash deals (EZJ.L Apollo 715p; 1788.HK HK$3.00 scheme), this file carries TWO layers: the three standalone scenarios here answer 'what is AES worth if the deal breaks', and the `corporate_action` block carries the deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting, which is the actionable number while the deal is live. The standalone `probability_weighted.weighted_iv` must NOT be read as the valuation signal on its own: the stock trades as merger arbitrage, and the $15.00 consideration is the effective ceiling on realisable value. Re-run this valuation the moment the merger closes (ticker dies; follow the AVB/EA precedent) or lapses (standalone becomes the only layer). FY0 is audited FY2025; Y1 is FY2026 with three quarters reported (9M revenue +14.7%, 9M attributable Adjusted EBITDA +34%), so the Y1 drivers are three-quarters actual. Standalone guidance was withdrawn after the merger agreement; backlog/capital-plan disclosures (12.0 GW signed backlog, 5.7 GW under construction, $4.2bn AES Indiana and $1.6bn AES Ohio 2026-28 capital plans) anchor the Y2-Y4 growth and capex paths.

bear.narrative: Deal breaks and the standalone capital-structure stress management itself described materialises: dividend cut and/or dilutive equity (modelled here as value destruction through higher AES-funded capex for longer and lower margins rather than a share-count change). 2025-Act FEOC restrictions and interconnection queues (4+ years) thin the post-2027 pipeline; new PPAs are signed without ITC/PTC support so attributable margin drifts to 25.5%; Chile/Colombia hydrology and Argentine peso devaluation recur; PREPA litigation drags; Ohio OCC rehearing imposes ring-fencing that traps utility cash. Terminal cap 15x reflects a market that will not pay a compounder multiple for a levered LatAm-exposed IPP.

base.growth_note: Y1 FY2026 +13.5%: 9M-2026 revenue +14.7% YoY with Q4-2025 (3,101) a soft comparator. Y2-Y4 7-8%: 5.7 GW under construction and 12.0 GW signed backlog (vs 34.7 GW installed) commissioning through 2029, double-digit rate-base growth at AES Indiana/Ohio, offset by the shrinking Energy Infrastructure (coal/gas pass-through) SBU. Fades to 2.5% by Y9.
base.margin_note: Attributable Adjusted EBITDA / consolidated revenue: FY2025 23.5%, 9M-2026 26.9% (2,815/10,474), FY2026E ~27.2% (Q4E ~960 on Q4-2025 769, in line with the +25-40% YoY run-rate of 2026 quarters). Rises to 29% by Y4 as high-margin contracted renewables/storage displace low-margin fuel pass-through generation, then held flat: no credit for margin beyond what the backlog mix implies.
base.capex_note: AES-funded capex (consolidated capex less partner funding): 9M-2026 37% of revenue -> Y1 36%. Declines as the 5.7 GW under construction is commissioned and the post-2025-Act pipeline slows: 20% by Y5, 13% terminal (= D&A 8.5% + ~4.5% growth capex consistent with 2.5% growth on attributable PP&E/revenue of ~1.8x).
base.tax_note: Cash tax 13% (FY2025 cash taxes paid $227m on ~$1.7bn attributable EBIT; retained ITC/PTC and transferability keep the cash rate low) ramping to 21% by Y10 as wind/solar credits phase out under the 2025 Act (storage ITC survives to 2033) and NCTI/GILTI changes raise US tax on Latin American earnings.
base.terminal_note: At 7.0% WACC / 2.5% g the Gordon value is ~22.8x terminal FCF; the 20x house cap binds. Implied terminal EV/EBITDA ~8x on attributable EBITDA -- below the ~9x forward multiple the consortium is paying, so the base does not assume a re-rating.

bull.narrative: Hyperscaler demand (Google Wilbarger County 20-yr co-located PPA, ~9 GW of direct hyperscaler PPAs, Monrovia Indiana data-centre campus) keeps the US pipeline converting at 2025's 4 GW/yr; backlog is fully safe-harboured so tax attributes persist to 2030+; AES Indiana/Ohio rate cases hold allowed ROEs; partner capital keeps funding ~45% of consolidated capex so AES-funded capex falls to 20% of revenue by Y4; attributable margin reaches 30.5% on renewables mix. Storage ITC through 2033 keeps the cash tax rate under 20%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: These weight the STANDALONE (deal-breaks) world only; the deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting lives in `corporate_action`. Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30% because management has said the standalone path likely requires a dividend cut and/or substantial equity issuance (capital-structure stress is exactly the trigger the method names), and because the renewables economics depend on tax-credit policy that the 2025 Act has already tightened. Bull cut to 20% because it needs hyperscaler demand, safe-harbour durability, rate-case outcomes and partner-capital availability to all hold at once. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: band_position is degenerate on this ticker and should be read as collapsed (null): SBC is 0.16% of revenue so house and street values differ by well under $1/share, and the market price sits far outside that band because it is pinned to the $15.00 deal consideration, not to either accounting regime.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
